title: Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters
summary: Given text s and a limit k, find the maximum length of a contiguous portion of s whose characters contain no more than k distinct values.
statement: Given text s and a limit k, find the maximum length of a contiguous portion of s whose characters contain no more than k distinct values.
constraints: Return the length of the longest contiguous substring containing AT MOST k distinct characters. Repeated occurrences count toward length; k=0 permits no nonempty substring.
hints: Expand a contiguous window and count how many distinct characters it contains.
When the count exceeds k, advance the left edge until the window is valid again.
Add the right character; while distinct>k decrement counts at left and delete zero counts. Update best with right-left+1.
Each index enters and leaves once. At most k+1 active character counts exist during an update, including k=0.
editorial: Maintain a valid sliding window with character frequencies. Shrinking only while there are too many distinct characters yields the longest valid window ending at each right position. Delete zero counts so dictionary size really counts distinct characters. The maximum across right endpoints is globally optimal. The oracle enumerates all substrings and measures explicit character sets.

tests.explanation: The substring ece has length 3 and uses only e and c. Extending it includes b, a third distinct character.
The best substring is bbbbb, of length 5. It starts after the beginning of the input.
